statement: Low friction (0.1–0.32) causes MISSED_GRASP because the current grip force (15 N) cannot generate enough normal force to hold the cube against tangential loads.
mechanism: Friction coefficient directly limits the maximum tangential force before slip (F_tangential ≤ μ * F_normal). With low μ, the 15 N grip force yields insufficient holding capacity, so the cube slips during the initial grasp or lift.
prediction: Increasing grip_force will reduce MISSED_GRASP failures in the low-friction region.

statement: Very small cubes (size_m 0.03–0.04 m) suffer high MISSED_GRASP rates due to limited contact area and sensitivity to sensor noise.
mechanism: Small cubes have less surface area for frictional contact and are more easily mislocalized by sensor noise, causing the fingers to miss or grasp poorly.
prediction: Increasing grasp_hold_steps (more time to stabilize the grasp) and adding retry_count (re-perception attempts) will lower MISSED_GRASP for the smallest cubes.

statement: High sensor noise (sensor_noise_m > 0.020) combined with very small cubes (size_m ≤ 0.038) creates extreme MISSED_GRASP rates due to large perception errors.
mechanism: Sensor noise above 2 cm causes the perceived cube position to deviate enough that the fingers miss the tiny cube entirely, and no retry is currently allowed to correct it.
prediction: Adding at least one retry (retry_count ≥ 1) will dramatically cut MISSED_GRASP in this high-noise, small-cube region.

statement: Long gripper delays (gripper_delay_steps 16–20) together with small cubes (size_m 0.03–0.0467) increase MISSED_GRASP because the cube can shift during the delay before the fingers close.
mechanism: The scenario-imposed delay between the grasp command and actual finger closure leaves the cube unheld for many physics steps; small cubes are more easily displaced by residual motion or noise.
prediction: Increasing grasp_hold_steps (ensuring a stable hold after closure) and/or grip_force (stronger squeeze) will reduce MISSED_GRASP in the high-delay, small-cube region.
